artifacts.summary: All 8 phases completed: production checker resolver and capability handshake, the verify-setting output gate with three honest states, the test-helper refactor onto the production resolver, gate documentation, a fresh trimmed-binary measurement confirming the out-of-band packaging route, and the item-3 ledger/direction-claim extensions across seven surfaces.

completion_data.completion_summary: Implemented the certifying-countermodel output gate (a 'verify' setting with three honest states rendered on every reported countermodel), the production checker resolver with a capability handshake and optional digest pinning, refactored the test differential tier onto that same resolver (incidentally speeding it up substantially), measured a trimmed checker binary to confirm the out-of-band opt-in packaging recommendation, and extended four ledger/coverage documents plus three test surfaces to state that the standing A2 tiers are UNSAT-direction evidence, not countermodel trust.

memory_candidates.content: In this codebase (ModelChecker), a theory's semantics class must never set an attribute literally named `verify` unless it truly implements the verify/falsify state-predicate pattern (logos/exclusion): models/semantic.py's initialize_with_state and iterate/models.py's generic model-rebuild path both branch on hasattr(semantics, 'verify') as the theory-capability test. Any other feature needing a setting called 'verify' must store its resolved value under a differently-named attribute (e.g. verify_mode) while keeping the settings dict key itself as 'verify' -- the collision only manifests during model iteration (a live, multi-solve test path), not on a plain single-solve construction, so it can pass ordinary unit tests and only surface in an integration/iteration test suite.

A leading-underscore helper function can be deliberately imported across modules within the same package for code-sharing purposes without being promoted to that module's public __all__ -- this codebase already has two instances of the pattern (certificate.py's window helpers imported by witness_constraints.py; semantic/checker.py's _invoke imported by tests/_lean_check.py). Document the reuse explicitly in both the source module's docstring and the consuming module's docstring so a future reader does not 'fix' the leading underscore by making the function harder to reach.

code/tests/ci/test_timing_marker_coverage.py is an AST-based project-wide gate: any test function that reads a real wall-clock (time.time/perf_counter/monotonic) AND asserts a bound comparison on the derived value must carry @pytest.mark.performance or @pytest.mark.xdist_serial, even if the operation being timed is itself monkeypatched to be instant/deterministic. When writing a new test with a 'confirms no hang' style elapsed-time assertion, add @pytest.mark.xdist_serial proactively rather than discovering the gate failure only when running the whole-project test suite.
